options.text: The two writings are the same prime factorisation of $90$, just with the repeated factor $3$ shown differently.
Report the words order of factors as the answer and stop.
The product $90$ produces the prime factors, so start from $90$ written as a single number and invent new primes.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Both writings use the primes 2, 3, 3, and 5; $3\times 3$ is the same as $3^{2}$, so they name the same unique prime factorisation.

teacher.key_rationale: Prime factorisation is unique up to order and how repeated primes are written. Naming the order label alone, or inventing new primes from the product numeral, misses that sameness.
